sam: Heads-up — seeing a spike in DNS resolution latency and a bunch of internal request timeouts between model-serving pods in us-west-2. Traces show a ~200-400ms stall during name resolution, then retries. Only affects a subset of nodes that have RDMA enabled.

infra-bot: [alert] High DNS latency (p95 ~ 350ms) for cluster us-west-2 on service: model-router — grafana: https://grafana.internal/redwood/d/abcd/dns-latency

priya: Can you paste coredns logs and the node-local-dns-cache logs from one of affected nodes? Also please run a quick tcpdump for UDP/53 on the node.

sam: grabbing logs now. coreDNS shows repeated: "read udp 10.0.0.12:42020->10.0.0.10:53: i/o timeout" and node-local-dns-cache has frequent connection resets. Running: `kubectl -n kube-system logs deployment/coredns --tail=200` and `tcpdump -n -s0 -w /tmp/dns-udp.pcap udp port 53`.

juan: possible MTU/fragmentation issue. AFAIK RDMA nodes were switched to jumbo frames (9000) last week, but overlay (calico/eni) might still be 1500 on the host route for pod traffic. Fragmented UDP to the DNS cluster -> some frags dropped by offloads -> timeouts. Have you checked `ip link show` and `calicoctl get felixconfig`?

olga: I grep'd kernel logs on one affected host — see lots of `UDP: bad checksum` and `ipfrag: reassembly failed` messages after the kernel update. Also saw `mlx5_core` messages on the RDMA NICs.

priya: That aligns. If DNS packets are getting fragmented, CoreDNS UDP handlers can miss queries. Quick repro: `iperf3 -u -c <coredns-pod-ip> -b 50M -l 4096` from a pod on an RDMA node to force fragmentation and watch logs.

sam: ran iperf3 test, reproduced fragmentation, CoreDNS logs show matching i/o timeouts. Also noticed kube-proxy conntrack count is high on these nodes: `conntrack -S` shows lots of UDP entries. Could be conntrack pressure + fragments = drops.

juan: Immediate mitigation options: 1) force DNS over TCP for pod resolvers (not ideal), 2) align MTUs (set host/pod MTU to 1500 on RDMA nodes or configure overlay for jumbo frames), 3) bump CoreDNS replicas and enable dns-over-tcp fallback (edit Corefile to include `max_concurrent 2000` and tcp settings).

olga: We pushed a quick config to calico to ensure VNI/encap path supports 9000 consistently on the RDMA host group, but that requires rolling those nodes which is disruptive. For quick reduction in errors I lowered RDMA host MTU back to 1500 on two canary nodes and restarted kubelet there. DNS timeouts dropped significantly.

priya: Good call. Also adjust node-local-dns-cache config: reduce cache TTL and enable `rejectedTTL` smaller so it doesn't keep negative entries for long while we fix fragmentation. Snapshot commands we used: ```
# check MTU
ip -o link show eth0
# check calico MTU
calicoctl get felixconfig default -o yaml | grep -i mtu
# tcpdump for fragments
tcpdump -n -i eth0 'udp[2:2] > 1400' -vv
```

sam: After lowering MTU on canaries and restarting node-local-dns-cache pod, internal calls successful. p95 DNS latency dropped from ~350ms -> ~20ms on those nodes.

infra-bot: [incident-note] Mitigation applied: RDMA host MTU set to 1500 on 2 canary hosts; node-local-dns-cache restarted; calico config updated for MTU validation. Ticket: #INC-2026-142.

juan: Next steps: schedule full rollout to RDMA fleet (or fix overlay to support jumbo reliably), run iperf + tcpdump validation pre/post change, and increase observability on fragment/dropped counters. Also add an alert for `CoreDNS i/o timeout` rate.

olga: I'll own the rollout plan and coordinate with Platform since rolling RDMA nodes requires careful GPU workload drain. Will add a preflight checklist: kernel/firmware versions, mlx5 driver, confirm calico MTU, drain window.

sam: thanks team. Opening a PR to add DNS-fragmentation playbook to runbook (how to repro, metrics to check, quick mitigation). For tracking, add to postmortem if incidence repeats. :thumbsup:
